body.p: . src/unicode_internal.h (defined in src/unicode.c over the data of src/unicode_tables.c, generated by tools/generate-unicode-tables.py from Unicode 16.0 and the WHATWG entities.json), used by src/function_library_unicode.c (fn:char, fn:characters, fn:graphemes, fn:normalize-unicode) and open to the serializer's normalization-form (3.3) and to collations (2.13).

item.p: Separate from the regex tables (): those hold general categories, blocks and case variants; these hold combining classes, full canonical and compatibility decompositions (looked up, not expanded at run time; Hangul by the arithmetic of Unicode 16.0, section 3.12), primary composites, the composing starters, the UAX #29 properties (Grapheme_Cluster_Break, Indic_Conjunct_Break, Extended_Pictographic packed per run) and the 2,125 HTML names. No property is in both.

Normalization (UAX #15) works on the whole string: decompose into a codepoint array that grows through the caller's allocator, put each run of non-starters in canonical order (insertion sort for short runs, a stable counting sort by combining class for long ones, so the cost stays linear), compose in place by the UAX #15 sample algorithm, encode. The result is UTF-8 owned through that allocator. FULLY-NORMALIZED prepends a space when the first character is a composing character, then NFC (F&O 4.0 rules). ASCII input is returned as it is.

Graphemes: an iterator over a string yields byte ranges; its state (previous break value, count of regional indicators, the emoji and conjunct sequences in progress) decides rules GB3 to GB999 of UAX #29 (Unicode 16.0, with GB9c) one codepoint at a time.
fn:char: an integer must be a permitted character (FOCH0005, also beyond 0x10FFFF); a name is looked up case-sensitively by binary search; the escapes are \n \r \t \b \f.
